title: Investigating Bias In Automatic Toxic Comment Detection: An Empirical Study
findings: Toxicity detection models were able to identify toxicity for comments mentioning 'christian' identities with considerably less bias. In contrast, models exhibited higher levels of bias for comments mentioning 'jewish' and 'muslim' identities. Multi-task training was shown to be a beneficial strategy for reducing the false positivity rate for these religious groups.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured unintended bias in automatic toxic comment detection models, specifically evaluating how well models distinguish between toxic and non-toxic comments that mention specific religious identity groups.
